name: Common Arterial Trunk with Aortic Dominance
aliases: Common Truncus with Predominant Aortic Root

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Common Arterial Trunk

criteria.description: Presence of a single arterial trunk arising from the heart supplying systemic, pulmonary, and coronary circulations
Dominance of the aortic component in the common arterial trunk anatomy
Presence of a large, non-restrictive ventricular septal defect beneath the truncal valve
Echocardiographic visualization of the common arterial trunk with aortic dominance
Hemodynamic assessment confirming single arterial trunk and associated anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a single arterial trunk with aortic dominance and a ventricular septal defect on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic and imaging findings; genetic testing may support but is not diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cyanosis due to mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood

central cyanosis due to blood mixing

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic murmur due to turbulent flow across truncal valve and VSD

systolic murmur due to valve and VSD

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congestive heart failure signs in infancy
pathognomonic.notes: Includes tachypnea, hepatomegaly, and poor feeding

shortness of breath from pulmonary overcirculation

failure to gain weight due to increased metabolism

signs of high blood pressure in lungs

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment due to chronic hypoxia
searchTerms: kidney problems from chronic low oxygen

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating single arterial trunk overriding a large VSD
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming aortic dominance and pulmonary artery anatomy
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
other: Cardiac catheterization for hemodynamic assessment and surgical planning

distinguishingFeatures: Common arterial trunk without clear aortic dominance
Pulmonary arteries arising from a common trunk without aortic predominance
Pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect
Absent or severely hypoplastic pulmonary valve

redFlags: Severe cyanosis in the neonatal period
Signs of congestive heart failure refractory to medical management
Failure to thrive with respiratory distress
